newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY TO SELL 30 PCT RABA STAKE AROUND SEPT-MTI.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY TO SELL 30 PCT RABA STAKE AROUND SEPT-MTI.

text.p: Hungary probably will offer at least a 30 percent stake in axle maker Raba this September at the earliest, Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha said on Friday.
The state would start the sale with a minimum 30 percent stake but it could rise to 88 percent by the end of Raba's privatisation process, official news agency MTI quoted Csiha.
She said the sale of the first stake would raise five to eight billion forints.

State Privatisation Agency APV Rt said in December it planned to acquire from the state-owned Hungarian Investment and Development Bank (MBFB) the 49.6 percent stake the bank currently holds in Raba through an equity swap and add this to APV's 32.3 percent stake.
The deal has not yet been completed.

Raba Rt said in December it expected its fifth consecutive year of profits in 1996 on the strength of an accelerating globalisation drive with over 27 billion forints in turnover and one billion forints in pre-tax profits.

The company, whose full name is Raba Magyar Vagon -es Gepgyar Rt, posted a pre-tax profit of 700 million forints on 23.7 billion forints in revenue in 1995 and a pre-tax profit of 547 million forints on 20.3 billion forints in revenue in 1994.

Raba, a supplier of major parts for the bus and truck industy, is Hungary's top exporter to the United States. Recently it started sales to Japan and Korea, while projects in China and Russia are underway.
